implementation.behavior: A reusable userspace batcher queries M156 backpressure before flush, blocks on FULL or unacknowledged LOSS, shrinks once per pressure observation, preserves partially completed entries, and grows only after four consecutive low-pressure NORMAL observations.
implementation.loss_recovery: LOSS remains fail-closed until the owning runtime explicitly acknowledges external drain/resynchronization through faisal_accel_batcher_acknowledge_loss().
implementation.bounds: Initial and maximum batch sizes are bounded to 1..AGI_LC_ACCEL_ACCOUNT_BATCH_MAX (64); entries must match the expected ABI size and device identity.
implementation.partial_completion: Completed entries are removed and unsent entries remain pending for retry; the library never silently discards an uncompleted entry.
implementation.security: The library does not grant authority, bypass capability checks, or treat model output as authorization; it only packages already-authorized lifecycle ioctl calls and fails closed on pressure or loss.

coverage: explicit loss acknowledgement after simulated drain
partial completion with retained pending entry

productivity_interpretation.benefit: The runtime can avoid futile submissions while the event ring is full or loss state is unacknowledged, retain partial work safely, and cautiously return toward larger batches after healthy observations.
productivity_interpretation.observed_adaptive_state: The deterministic unit run moved through four flushes, ten pressure queries, three detected loss/backpressure events, and ended at target batch size one.
productivity_interpretation.raw_throughput_scope: The integrated gate also measured the inherited M155 batch workload at speedup_x100=137 in this QEMU run, but this single run does not isolate M157’s causal contribution and is not a physical accelerator claim.

build_artifact.kernel_source: M156 kernel image reused; M157 is userspace runtime/test integration.

release_gate.reason: M157 is bounded userspace/QEMU validation. Physical accelerator qualification, independent reproducible production builders, signed artifacts, stable/LTS forward-port qualification, and external security governance remain required.
release_gate.hardware_claim: No physical GPU, NPU, VRAM, IOMMU, DMA, vendor-driver, reset, or fleet qualification is claimed.

known_limitations: Adaptive control is implemented as a reusable userspace library; it does not autonomously drain the event ring or decide semantic resynchronization.
Loss acknowledgement is intentionally explicit because only the owning runtime can verify that its world-state or telemetry consumer has resynchronized.
The unit test uses an injected ioctl model for deterministic state-machine coverage; QEMU validates integration and packaging, not physical accelerator behavior.
No independent M157-only raw-throughput improvement is claimed; the M155 benchmark is retained as supporting context.
The kernel remains based on the Linux v7.2-rc7 development line and production release qualification remains incomplete.
